episode_title: ReStructured Summer Sizzle: Our Complex Relationship with Productivity

real_qa.q: What does Melissa Terito mean by defining productivity individually, and why should people stop feeling guilty about rest?
real_qa.r: You have to define individually what productive means for you and stop feeling guilty. Most people listening to the podcast deserve a Sunday in pajamas until 3 p.m., and not every day needs to be at an intensity level of 10 out of 10 to be considered productive.

real_qa.q: How does Melissa Terito intentionally structure her work week to avoid burnout?
real_qa.r: Melissa intentionally plans her weeks so that Tuesdays and Thursdays are five to seven meeting days with high intensity, while other days like Wednesday have no meetings scheduled. This deliberate planning prevents her from running a rat race every single day and wearing herself out repeatedly.
real_qa.requete: Melissa Terito meeting schedule productivity structure

real_qa.q: Why is Melissa Terito taking a 30-day sabbatical in August despite potential judgment?
real_qa.r: Melissa is taking a 30-day sabbatical in August and acknowledges that some people may question the need for it or view it negatively. She emphasizes the importance of defining productivity individually rather than succumbing to external judgment about rest and recovery.
